exposure: Mode of birth (spontaneous vaginal birth, emergency cesarean, elective cesarean)
Type of professionals assisting the birth
outcome: Women's perceptions of the quality of maternal and newborn care (QMNC)
cohort: The study included 620 women who completed an anonymous online survey about their perceptions of maternal and newborn care received in hospitals in Romania during the COVID-19 pandemic.
finding: The study found significant gaps in the quality of maternal and newborn care in Romanian hospitals during the COVID-19 pandemic, with births by cesarean being the most affected across various quality indicators.
mod_finding: Cesarean births, both elective and emergency, were associated with more frequent lack of early breastfeeding, skin-to-skin contact, rooming-in, and exclusive breastfeeding at discharge compared to spontaneous vaginal birth, with emergency cesareans consistently showing lower quality of care across most domains.
